text:
aj: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for incremental billing reconciliation window. TL;DR: move from batch nightly reconciliation to per-tenant incremental manifests + watermarking to close gaps faster. Seeking tradeoffs and edge-case callouts.

maya: big +1 on reducing time-to-detect billing gaps. main worry: late-arriving tokens from async sinks (e.g., edge ingestion retries). how do you plan to handle out-of-order events?

aj: good point. thinking: each tenant writes a monotonically increasing sequence_id in events and we emit an hourly "manifest" that summarizes [max_seq, min_ts, count, checksum]. reconciliation consumer compares manifests and fetches missing seq ranges for audit. late events can be appended to a "late bucket" with tombstone/repair markers.

lorenzo: sequence_id helps. two quick things: 1) we need idempotent ingestion path (dedupe by event_id) or seq holes will be ambiguous; 2) manifests must be compact — avoid full bloom per-tenant every hour. a small sketch:
```
manifest: { tenant_id, window_start, window_end, max_seq, compact_cksum }
repair_event: { tenant_id, seq_from, seq_to, records: [] }
```

sarah: operational concerns: how does this impact storage & query cost for audits? If repairs include full records we might double storage. maybe store only pointers (s3 path) + small audit index. Also retention: audits must be available for 90 days (legal), then compact.

aj: agreed. plan: manifests + pointers to event batches (parquet blobs) in long-term store. repair events only include pointers; a separate repair fetch job materializes and writes a repair manifest for auditor use. keep raw events for 90d then transition to compressed.

maya: what about attribution complexity — a single request can span multiple tokens and model variants (hosted vs dedicated). The meter needs to attribute token counts to correct billing unit. Does seq_id live at request granularity or token-event granularity?

lorenzo: sequence per billing-event (tokenized chunk) preferred: that makes backfills precise. request-level seq would need per-request expansion to tokens for repairs which is messy. cost: more events, but compact batch storage mitigates that.

aj: yep leaning token-granularity events. we can keep a request_id field on each token event to allow grouping. attribution rules run in the reconciliation consumer and emit per-tenant per-billing-unit deltas.

billing-bot: FYI: nightly invoice generator currently reads "aggregate_tokens" table. switching to near-real-time will require a compatibility shim for invoices until cutover.

aj: thanks @billing-bot — action: I'll coordinate a compatibility API that serves aggregates computed from manifests for the invoice generator during migration.

maya: one more: time-window semantics. If we use hourly manifests, what about tenants with very low throughput? Hourly may delay detection. Maybe hybrid: emit manifest when count threshold or time threshold reached.

lorenzo: agreed — hybrid watermark: manifest when (count>=N) OR (time>=T). Also include a soft watermark for very-late events to avoid infinite waiting.

aj: sounds good. I'll draft an RFC with: event schema, manifest format, dedupe rules, repair protocol, storage plan, retention/compaction, migration path for invoice system.

sarah: please include SLO targets for reconciliation lag and repair closure time in the RFC. ops will need runbooks for large backfills.

aj: will do. timeline: draft by EOD Fri, request review next week.

maya: thanks — if the RFC sketches the failure modes + Spike plan for a prototype, I'm happy to help implement the consumer.

lorenzo: I'll take the dedupe/ingest side; will add a small test harness to simulate late events.

aj: assigned. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
